skill.name: database-operations
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants to write SQLAlchemy database operations with bulk methods, SQL joins, and repository classes.
skill.summary: Encourages efficient SQLAlchemy queries and repository-based database access.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The static system reconnaissance finding is a false positive. SKILL.md only provides SQLAlchemy guidance about bulk operations, joins, and repository classes, with no executable code, prompt injection, or data collection intent.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid for-loops. Instead always prefer bulk operations using SQLAlchemy's built-in methods or use

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 6 recommends SQLAlchemy bulk operations and SQL joins for efficient database access. It does not request system reconnaissance, host inspection, command execution, or sensitive data collection.

content.value_statement: Database code can become slow or hard to maintain when queries are repeated in loops. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward bulk SQLAlchemy operations and repository classes.
actual_capabilities: Encourages SQLAlchemy bulk operations instead of per-row loops.
Promotes SQL joins for related data in a single query.
Directs database logic into repository classes.
Provides concise guidance for efficient and maintainable database code.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, examples, or helper functions.
Does not define transaction, migration, indexing, or connection management rules.
Does not inspect an existing schema or verify query performance.
Does not replace application-specific database review or testing.

use_cases.title: Refactor ORM Queries
use_cases.description: Use the skill when converting row-by-row database code into bulk SQLAlchemy operations or join-based queries.

use_cases.title: Review Repository Boundaries
use_cases.description: Use it to check whether database access stays inside repository classes during code review.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Generation
use_cases.description: Use it to instruct Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to produce maintainable database operation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Query Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQLAlchemy code for efficient database operations. Focus on bulk methods, SQL joins, and repository class boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Loop-Based Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the database access in the selected files to avoid per-row loops. Prefer SQLAlchemy bulk operations or join-based queries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Repository Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Design repository class methods for this feature. Keep database operations inside repositories and explain the query strategy before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Data Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this data workflow for query efficiency, repository boundaries, and maintainability. Flag loop-driven database operations and propose safer SQLAlchemy patterns.

output_examples.input: Review this SQLAlchemy feature branch for database operation issues.
output_examples.output: The response identifies repeated database access in loops, recommends bulk operations, and suggests moving direct model queries into repository methods.

output_examples.input: Help design database access for a new reporting feature.
output_examples.output: The response outlines repository methods, join-based query planning, and places database behavior behind a clear data access boundary.

output_examples.input: Check whether this service layer follows database access guidance.
output_examples.output: The response flags direct database operations outside repositories and recommends clearer ownership for SQLAlchemy query logic.

best_practices: Use the skill before generating or reviewing SQLAlchemy data access code.
Ask for repository boundaries and query strategy in the same request.
Pair AI suggestions with tests and database performance checks.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a substitute for schema-specific performance analysis.
Requesting direct model queries across service layers.
Accepting loop-driven database writes without reviewing bulk alternatives.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides AI tools to write SQLAlchemy database operations that favor bulk methods, joins, and repository classes.

faq.question: Does it execute database queries?
faq.answer: No. It contains instructions only and does not include scripts or runtime code.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it optimize every query?
faq.answer: No. It gives general guidance and still needs schema-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Is it only for SQLAlchemy?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for SQLAlchemy database operations.

faq.question: Does it include migration guidance?
faq.answer: No. It does not cover migrations, indexes, transactions, or connection management in detail.
